streetView.conditionNotes: Roof appears to be in good condition with uniform shingle coloration and no visible missing or damaged sections. Dimensional shingles appear intact across all visible planes.
streetView.notes: Single-story ranch-style home with a complex hip roof system featuring multiple intersecting planes. Brick and stone exterior. Roof pitch appears moderate (approximately 4:12 to 6:12). The multi-plane hip configuration will increase labor complexity and material waste factor for any future replacement. Low-slope transitions between roof sections should be inspected for flashing integrity. No gutters are visible from this street-view angle, which may be a concern for drainage management given the wide eave lines. Driveway and property suggest higher-end residential construction.

satellite.notes: Large complex hip roof with multiple wings creating numerous inside and outside corners. Total interior linear feet = 342ft, which is somewhat below the 396-576ft sanity range for 18 facets — the south and west wing junctions are partially obscured by shadow, making precise enumeration of all sub-facet hips difficult. Ridge proportion = 60/342 = 17.5%, within the expected 10-25% range. The roof appears in good condition with no visible damage, uniform medium-gray asphalt shingle color throughout. Driveway/turnaround visible to north. Lawn area well-maintained around perimeter.
